p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Stereotyping is a type of generalization which attributes traits or characteristics to everyone in a large group. People who stereotype tend to have fixed and unbending opinions. They respond to challenges by distorting reality, rather than reconsider their assumptions and conclusions, which they have labelled as the truth. What happens is that the facts are compared to the stereotype and then rejected, because they do not fit the stereotype. Stereotyping is often caused by ethno-centrism. The ramifications of stereotyping are that it forces us to choose sides, causes destructive competition, alienates us from others and leads to narrow thinking. We end up denying dignity to others, whom we stereotype, and generate unhappiness all around us.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: For decades, sanitation programmes measured success by the number of toilets constructed. Contractors were paid per unit, officials reported the totals and villages were declared covered. Surveys conducted a few years later often found a different picture: many toilets used as storerooms for grain or firewood, others abandoned because the pit had filled and no one knew how to empty it, and family members, particularly men, continuing to defecate in the open out of long habit. The structures existed; the change in behaviour they were meant to represent did not.

The lesson, learned at considerable expense, is that sanitation is a social practice rather than a piece of hardware. Habits formed over a lifetime are not altered by the appearance of a concrete cubicle in the backyard. Programmes that succeeded tended to begin with conversation rather than construction, helping a community see for itself how faecal contamination travelled from open fields to drinking water and food, and to children's stomachs. Once a village resolved collectively to end open defecation, households often built toilets with little subsidy and, crucially, used them. Maintenance, too, required planning: arrangements for emptying pits, water within reach and designs suited to local soil. None of this diminishes the importance of building toilets. It simply insists that a toilet counted is not the same as a toilet used.

questions.q: People who stereotype are NOT likely to
opts: treat their opinions as the truth
questions.why: They distort reality 'rather than reconsider their assumptions'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Which phrase means the same as "alienates"?
questions.why: Vocabulary. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to "ramification"?
questions.why: Vocabulary: a ramification is a (usually unwelcome) consequence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Planning Officer), Apr 2023.

questions.q: Which title best suits the passage?
opts: The Rising Cost of Construction Contracts
Beyond Bricks: Sanitation as a Change in Behaviour
How to Build a Cheap Toilet
questions.why: Main idea: 'sanitation is a social practice rather than a piece of hardware'; 'a toilet counted is not the same as a toilet used'.

questions.q: According to later surveys, many toilets built under earlier programmes were:
opts: used as storerooms for grain or firewood.
questions.why: Detail: 'many toilets used as storerooms for grain or firewood'; men in fact continued to defecate in the open.

questions.q: The author implies that paying contractors per toilet:
opts: encouraged a focus on construction numbers rather than actual use.
was the main reason later programmes succeeded.
made toilets too expensive for households.
ensured that every toilet was properly used.
questions.why: Inference: payment 'per unit' fitted a system that 'measured success by the number of toilets constructed', while 'the change in behaviour... did not' occur.

questions.q: The sentence 'None of this diminishes the importance of building toilets' serves to:
opts: argue that toilet construction should be stopped.
cast doubt on the findings of the surveys.
clarify that the author objects not to construction but to treating it as sufficient.
questions.why: Purpose: the next sentence explains the real point: 'a toilet counted is not the same as a toilet used'.

questions.q: As used in the passage, 'crucially' means:
opts: in a way that is decisively important
in a harsh and cruel way
questions.why: Vocabulary: that households 'crucially, used them' marks use as the essential outcome.
